chapter: Los Angeles in 1935: school, jam sessions and the hobo trip west
title: Hardships in Texas and pool-shooting Rooster
summary: Recalls shooting pool with Rooster and his traveling partner Quincy Forks.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you -- you didn't stay in Texas, did you?
No, we had some real hardships in Texas. That was like the year of Grapes of Wrath, like when -- the dust storms... (recording interrupted). End of Reel 1
You were about to tell me about your hardships in Amarillo, Texas.

Yes. My traveling partner and I, we had learned to shoot pool at an early age. As I said, we used to hobo over to Oklahoma City and watch this boy named Rooster shoot pool and never went to school, and Charlie Christian played the guitar.
Now, Rooster came out here and was playing Bill "Bojangles" for money, people was thinking, you know. He would go downtown with all kinds of money.
No. No one ever knew. His name was Rooster. But he looked like Joe Louis. That size, build, face, features, everything.
